items.new: And the women of New Bedford bloom like their own red roses. But roses bloom only in summer; the fine carnation of their cheeks is perennial as sunlight in the seventh heaven. Nowhere else can you match that bloom — except in Salem, where they say the young girls breathe such musk that their sailor sweethearts can smell them miles offshore, as if they were approaching the fragrant Moluccas instead of the Puritan sands.

Wrapping myself in my shaggy bearskin jacket, I fought my way through the stubborn storm. Inside, I found a small, scattered congregation of sailors and sailors' wives and widows. A muffled silence reigned, broken only at times by the shrieks of the storm. Each worshipper seemed deliberately sitting apart from the others, as if each grief were an island, incommunicable. The chaplain hadn't arrived yet. These silent islands of men and women sat steadfastly gazing at several marble tablets with black borders, set into the walls on either side of the pulpit. items.new: While he spoke these words, the howling of the shrieking, slanting storm outside seemed to add new power to the preacher. Describing Jonah's storm, he seemed tossed by a storm himself. His deep chest heaved like a ground swell; his tossed arms seemed the warring elements at work; and the thunder rolling from his dark brow and the light leaping from his eyes made every simple listener watch him with a strange, quick fear.

items.new: "Shipmates, God has laid only one hand upon you; both His hands press upon me. I have read you, by whatever murky light may be mine, the lesson that Jonah teaches to all sinners; and so to you, and still more to me, for I am a greater sinner than you. And now how gladly would I come down from this masthead and sit on the hatches there where you sit, and listen as you listen, while one of you reads to me that other and more awful lesson which Jonah teaches to me, as a pilot of the living God. How, being an anointed pilot-prophet, or speaker of true things, and commanded by the Lord to sound those unwelcome truths in the ears of a wicked Nineveh, Jonah, appalled at the hostility he would raise, fled from his mission, and tried to escape his duty and his God by taking ship at Joppa. But God is everywhere; Tarshish he never reached. As we have seen, God came upon him in the whale, and swallowed him down to living gulfs of doom, and with swift slantings tore him along 'into the midst of the seas,' where the eddying depths sucked him ten thousand fathoms down, and 'the weeds were wrapped about his head,' and all the watery world of woe bowled over him. Yet even then, beyond the reach of any plummet — 'out of the belly of hell' — when the whale grounded on the ocean's utmost bones, even then God heard the engulfed, repenting prophet when he cried. Then God spoke to the fish; and from the shuddering cold and blackness of the sea, the whale came breaching up toward the warm and pleasant sun, and all the delights of air and earth; and 'vomited out Jonah upon the dry land'; when the word of the Lord came a second time; and Jonah, bruised and beaten — his ears, like two seashells, still multitudinously murmuring of the ocean — Jonah did the Almighty's bidding. And what was that, shipmates? To preach the Truth to the face of Falsehood! That was it!

items.new: When I interrupted him, he put the idol away. Soon he went to the table, picked up a large book, placed it on his lap, and began counting the pages with careful regularity. At every fiftieth page — as I imagined — he'd stop, look vaguely around, and let out a long, gurgling whistle of astonishment. Then he'd start again at the next fifty, seeming to begin at one each time, as if he couldn't count past fifty — and it was only the sheer number of fifties that amazed him.

items.new: We grew so wide awake that lying down became tiresome. Little by little we sat up, bedclothes tucked snugly around us, leaning against the headboard with our four knees drawn up close together and our two noses bent over them, as if our kneecaps were warming pans. We felt wonderfully cozy, especially since it was so cold outside — and outside the blankets too, since there was no fire in the room. To truly enjoy bodily warmth, some small part of you must be cold, because no quality in this world exists except by contrast. Nothing exists in itself. If you flatter yourself that you've been comfortable all over for a long time, then you can no longer be said to be comfortable at all. But if, like Queequeg and me in that bed, only the tip of your nose or the crown of your head is slightly chilled, then in your general consciousness you feel most delightfully and unmistakably warm. For this reason, a bedroom should never have a fire — that's one of the luxurious discomforts of the rich. The height of this kind of bliss is having nothing but the blanket between your warmth and the cold outside air. Then you lie like the one warm spark in the heart of an arctic crystal.

items.new: We had been sitting hunched like this for some time when all at once I decided to open my eyes. When I'm between sheets, day or night, awake or asleep, I tend to keep my eyes shut to concentrate the snugness of being in bed. Because no person can truly feel their own identity unless their eyes are closed — as if darkness were the proper element of our essence, though light suits our clay better. Opening my eyes and leaving my own pleasant, self-created darkness for the imposed, coarse outer gloom of an unlit midnight, I felt a disagreeable jolt. Nor did I object at all when Queequeg hinted that perhaps we had better light a lamp, since we were wide awake and he badly wanted a few quiet puffs from his tomahawk pipe. I should mention that although I'd been so against his smoking in bed the night before, see how elastic our stiff prejudices become once love starts to bend them. Now I liked nothing better than having Queequeg smoke beside me — even in bed — because he seemed so full of serene, domestic contentment. I no longer worried about the landlord's fire insurance. I was alive only to the condensed, confidential comfort of sharing a pipe and a blanket with a real friend. With our shaggy jackets around our shoulders, we passed the tomahawk pipe back and forth until a blue hanging canopy of smoke slowly gathered above us, lit by the flame of the newly lit lamp.

items.new: His story finished with his pipe's last dying puff. Queequeg embraced me, pressed his forehead against mine, and blowing out the light, we rolled away from each other, this way and that, and were soon asleep.

items.new: Two enormous wooden pots painted black, hung by asses' ears, swung from the cross-trees of an old topmast planted in front of an old doorway. The horns of the cross-trees had been sawed off on the other side, so that this old topmast looked not a little like a gallows. Perhaps I was oversensitive to such impressions at the time, but I could not help staring at this gallows with a vague misgiving. I got a sort of crick in my neck as I gazed up at the two remaining horns — yes, two of them, one for Queequeg and one for me. It's ominous, I think. A Coffin for my innkeeper on landing in my first whaling port; tombstones staring at me in the whalemen's chapel; and here a gallows! And a pair of prodigious black pots too! Are these last throwing out oblique hints about Tophet, that biblical place of fire?
